key_insight: Biology-guided transcriptomic features outperformed unstable gene-level selection for predicting atezolizumab response in advanced urothelial carcinoma.
clinical_relevance: Transcriptomic profiling appears most useful when it adds to established clinical and biomarker data through interpretable pathway-level features rather than sparse gene lists.
method: Compared knowledge-guided tumor microenvironment gene-set features with data-driven transcriptome-wide gene selection.
Evaluated incremental predictive value over clinical variables, standard biomarkers, and research-enriched biomarkers.
Assessed stability across folds and tested the approach in an external evaluation set.
evidence_signal: In IMvigor210 (298 patients), knowledge-guided features improved AUPRC by 0.058 over clinical variables alone and still showed smaller gains over biomarker-enriched baselines; external evaluation showed a similar advantage.
watch_item: Data-driven gene selection was unstable across folds, so transcriptomic signatures may not generalize well without biologically informed representation and external validation.
paper_title: Incremental Predictive Value and Representation of Transcriptomic Features for Immunotherapy Response in Advanced Urothelial Carcinoma
